summary_en: This study tests tepotinib combined with ivonescimab in non-small cell lung cancer that has MET exon 14 skipping and is advanced or recurrent. Tepotinib is taken by mouth at 225 mg or 450 mg once daily, and ivonescimab is given through an IV every 3 weeks, for up to 24 months of ivonescimab treatment. The study focuses on safety and finding the best tepotinib dose with few or mild side effects; a formal primary outcome is not stated, and it is a Phase 1 pilot study.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa tepotinib combinado con ivonescimab en cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas con salto del exón 14 de MET que es avanzado o recurrente. El tepotinib se toma por vía oral a 225 mg o 450 mg una vez al día, y el ivonescimab se administra por vena cada 3 semanas, durante hasta 24 meses de tratamiento con ivonescimab. El estudio se enfoca en la seguridad y en encontrar la mejor dosis de tepotinib con pocos efectos secundarios o leves; no se indica un resultado principal formal, y es un estudio piloto de fase 1.
who_for: Pathologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer.
MET exon 14 skipping confirmed by an FDA-approved assay in a certified lab.
Advanced or recurrent disease with measurable disease by RECIST 1.1.
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status of 2 or less.
Adequate blood counts, kidney, liver and clotting function as defined by the study.
not_for: Other actionable alterations such as EGFR, ALK, ROS1, RET, KRAS, HER2 or BRAF V600E.
Prior angiogenesis inhibitor therapy, such as bevacizumab or ramucirumab.
Untreated or active brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease, unless specific conditions are met.
Interstitial lung disease requiring steroid treatment, or prior grade 3 or higher immune-related side effect.
Recent serious bleeding, clotting, heart events, or inflammatory bowel disease within the stated time windows.
